implementerProof.how: This round's head is a forward merge and a migration renumber: main landed its own 0150_dpop_proofs while this branch held 0150-0159, and the repository numbers its migration set 1 to N with no gap, so this branch's block moved to 0151-0160. The implementer's forward-merge comment reports the fingerprint changed, so this is a full test round and every proof was taken again. All of them hold at the renumbered head: the census reads schema 150 and the ten pending migrations 0151-0160 and answers ok; protocol 1's pairs all pass; protocol 2, measured with both sides in one window, is lower after for every statement; A9 is faster on all six routes with nothing near the bound; and the reads answer over HTTP as the pull request says. The one thing that is not green is a check the branch does not touch (below).

failures.criterion: CI green at the head, which the merge gate needs.
failures.evidence: At the code head eee7b2d6, 27 checks pass, one is skipped, the ci-ok aggregator is still queued and pi-legion fails on one test: '(fail) a role's deep-worker runs in the background: the task call returns before it ends, a message sent meanwhile is read, and the job's result wakes the role [4112.05ms]' (job 124744259239). It is not this change: packages/pi-legion, packages/pi-shared and packages/pi-envoy are byte for byte what main carries at the merge's main parent 072a7d344 (git diff --stat over those three paths between 072a7d344 and eee7b2d6 prints nothing), the test belongs to main's own background-jobs feature (#2571, d0e8971b), and that lane is red on main itself at c5df57399 while green at 527853ab1 and f0fd4dfb7 - a flaky four-second timing test. The remedy is a re-run of that one job, which is not the tester's to make: this phase reads CI and re-runs no lane. Nothing else at the head is red.

proof.observed: Before against after (the after side's three readings in order): listIssueAsksQueryAll 6.057ms -> 376us; listIssueRootMessagesQuery 3.845ms -> 74us; searchQuery keywords only 201.092ms -> 75.604ms and 72.841ms; searchQueryMeaning 1.186199s -> 1.088632s and 1.047644s; relatedKeywordQuery 4.301821s -> 4.343509s and 4.223474s; relatedMeaningQuery 5.40049s -> 5.615452s and 5.310966s; relatedProbeSQL 3.878ms -> 3.089ms and 2.978ms. listArtifactAsksQueryOpen 1.629ms -> 2.848ms is the one that rises, which is this change's ordered drop of asks_open_artifact and not a changed statement: the branch edits only its comment.

They are flat rather than improved, which is what the pull request's own R2 reading says they must be: after the change their time is in the meaning arms' embedding reads, 38.7 per cent of the plan in one Index Scan using embeddings_pkey, not in the document arm this change moved. The document arm's own statements - the keyword search at a third of its time and the probe at four fifths - are where the gain shows.

proof.criterion: A9, the write bound: the median of 50 requests to each of the five write routes R10 names, and an upload over a 100-660 KB document, rises by no more than 10%.
proof.surface: Two copies of one seed, so both sides carry the same history: main's own server, built from the merge's main parent 072a7d344, against a copy at main's schema 150, and this head's server against a copy its migrations took to 160. Both uploads write documents the harness created through the API with the same bytes on both sides (8,019 and 600,019); the head's one-off full related-terms build was waited out before its runs, since round 3 showed it inflates every route while it runs.

Round 2 of this phase shows what an unequal fixture does to this measurement (+10% to +19% on comments with 1,709 comments on one side against 903 on the other), which is why both sides here are copies of one seed.

notes: The measurement Postgres is Job infra-325-postgres-wb4f6 in the builds namespace and must be deleted when the last measurement is done: kubectl -n builds delete job infra-325-postgres-wb4f6, which takes its Service with it. It now holds the seeded original at main's schema and three copies of it: the base side, the head side the write routes drove, and an untouched head copy the statements are read on. The pod's own volume is wiped at every pod replacement, but the Job is not, so a replacement pod rebuilds its URL from the Job's env and Service.

The pod now carries a test Postgres of its own (LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN, 18.6) whose role is no superuser, so three store census tests and the people tests cannot run there. A private cluster of the same version is one initdb away in the pod (/usr/lib/postgresql/18/bin is on the image), which is what this round used; an earlier round's hand-built Postgres 17 under /legion/scratch/pg is no longer needed.

Only one thing is red at this head and it is main's: the pi-legion lane's background-jobs test. The three plugin packages are byte for byte main's at the merge parent, and the same lane is red on main at c5df57399 and green at two later main commits. A re-run of that job is all it needs.
